correctness.rationale: The VC upper bound uses each shattered query x_i to obtain a distinct prime with strictly largest exponent at x_i, all dividing a common positive-label hypothesis y<=N; the k smallest distinct primes thus have product <=N. Queries at those primes and hypotheses equal to selected products give the lower bound. The exact bitset recursive game W_N(H,d) checks existence of an adaptive full binary mistake tree by enumerating all x>=2 and both nonempty depth-(d-1) version spaces; cardinality pruning uses the necessary 2^d distinct leaves. Monotonicity of [N] then converts each pair of false/true neighboring N into a least threshold. Independent bitset dynamic programming reproduced false at (319,6),(1279,7),(1280,8), true at (320,6),(1280,7), and all five earlier threshold boundary pairs. The actual witness.json was read and independently checked: 128 distinct valid leaf hypotheses of depth seven and every root-to-leaf divisibility decision. This proves the finite cutoff with an exhaustive finite certificate, not an infinite formula for all deeper thresholds.

value.rationale: This is a natural, directly motivated separation of two fundamental learning-theoretic dimensions for the elementary arithmetic divisibility predicate. The exact first occurrence of gap three, including its two adjacent negative certificates and fully explicit 128-leaf adaptive witness, is a meaningful finite structural threshold. It neither renames a generic inequality nor claims unsupported later-depth completeness.

final_claim: For the concept class h_y(x)=1 exactly when x divides y, with both x,y in {1,...,N}, VC dimension is the largest k with the k-th primorial <=N. The first N supporting Littlestone depths 1,...,7 are 2,4,9,27,81,320,1280. In particular L_1280=7, V_1280=4, and 1280 is the first gap of at least three.
limitations: Only finite initial segment of positive integers and exact divisibility queries; finite Ldim thresholds proved only through depth seven.
No general formula for eighth or later Littlestone thresholds; tests at N=1280 do not establish infinite impossibility.
